title: Convert --toolchain_resolution_debug to take a regex of toolchain typ…

timeline.message:
Convert --toolchain_resolution_debug to take a regex of toolchain types to debug

Work towards #12110.
Fixes #7713.
timeline.author: John Cater

diff.patch:
@@ -148,13 +148,15 @@ public class PlatformOptions extends FragmentOptions {

       name = "toolchain_resolution_debug",
-      defaultValue = "false",
+      defaultValue = "-.*",
+      converter = RegexFilter.RegexFilterConverter.class,

timeline.body:
…es to debug

Work towards #12110.
Fixes #7713.

RELNOTES: The flag `--toolchain_resolution_debug` now takes a regex argument, which is used to check which toolchain types should have debug info printed. You may use `.*` as an argument to keep the current behavior of debugging every toolchain type.

timeline.body: If this is empty, is there any actual information to debug? i..e what gets printed when this returns true and the input is empty?

reply.body:
Even targets with no toolchains will have an execution platform selected (and this is used in some tests).

Ideally we could instead do `--toolchain_resolution_debug=//some/configured:target`, but that would require ConfiguredTargetFunction to make the check and pass a debug flag, thus complicating the ToolchainContextKey even more.

timeline.body: Does plain old `--toolchain_resolution_debug` still work? (as an alias for `.*`)?

reply.body: No, the argument is required (and if it is skipped an error will be printed). I couldn't figure out a way to distinguish between no flag being passed, and a base `--toolchain_resolution_debug` with no argument in order to keep the current behavior unchanged.
